claims.statement: In 1876 Tom Allen had about $25,000 but lost most of it making a book in England.
Tom Allen said he was holding over $600 in stakes on the Rigal and Carteron match.
Tom Allen refereed the wrestling match between Carteron and Rigal at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, which went undecided after a severe struggle on Tuesday evening.
Tom Allen ruled that the match between Carteron and Rigal would have its final decision on Thursday evening, February 10, 1876, at the same hour and place.
Tom Allen played a legitimate part in the crib scene from Tom and Jerry at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, a couple of weeks before April 1876.
Friends of Tom Allen met to raise money to buy back the belt won from Mike McCoole and present it to Allen.
Theobald Bauer and Andre Christol volunteered to wrestle at Tom Allen's benefit, with the winner to receive a massive silver goblet from Allen; Wilhelm Beyer was to referee.
Tom Allen was to be presented with the disputed McCoole belt at his benefit on March 30, 1876.
Tom Allen objected when Joe Coburn was billed in St. Louis as the 'Champion of the World'.
Tom Allen introduced Prof. Bauer and Herr Heygster to the audience at the Temple, St. Louis, before their second wrestling match.
During the recess Tom Allen announced that a silver belt, which Bauer's friends had obtained for him as champion Greco-Roman wrestler of America, would be presented to Bauer.
Tom Allen received a dispatch from Jem Coyne of Newark, N.J., announcing that Joe Goss had arrived in America.
Tom Allen was a guest, with Prof. Bauer, Andre Christol and Leon Schuler, at a breakfast given by the French caterer Jean Bonnet in St. Louis.
Bauer said he would return to St. Louis and make a match with Julius Schroeder once Tom Allen notified him that a suitable deposit had been posted.
Tom Allen said he knocked Ned Donnelly down on Tuesday, 11 April, after Donnelly sneered when Allen asked whether he would break their engagement.
Tom Allen appeared for the wrestler Bauer and put up the money for him, Bauer's $250 deposit for a wrestling match with Schroeder at the Temple.
Tom Allen acted for Prof. Bauer at Tony Faust's, depositing the remainder of the stakes for Bauer's match with Julius Schroeder.
Tom Allen was empowered to sign articles of agreement for Prof. Bauer's match with Julius Schroeder.
Tom Allen said he had been chosen referee for the wrestling match between Thiebaud Bauer and Julius Schroeder at the Temple.
Tom Allen came on stage with the lightweight champions Arthur Chambers and Billy Edwards and introduced them to the audience.
Ben De Bar stood by Tom Allen at the signing and put up Allen's money.
Before the Goss fight, Tom Allen was told he could not win and asked whether Eph Holland was square in his dealings.
Tom Allen trained at Cedar Park, a retreat near Carthage owned by John Young, under the care of Jack Madden.
Tom Allen began active training on the Monday before the interview.
Joe Goss said the coming fight with Tom Allen will be one of the hardest ever known in the annals of the ring.
Tom Allen published an apology (amende honorable) admitting that he had written unjust criticism for the New York Clipper (printed as 'urjust str'ctures').
Tom Allen wrote a full apology to the New York Clipper, which had excluded his name from its columns for nearly four years after a card he wrote.
Tom Allen acted as referee for the Bauer-Miller wrestling championship match at Wood's Theater in Cincinnati on August 29, 1876.
Tom Allen appeared as referee at the Bauer-Miller wrestling match in Cincinnati on August 29, 1876.
Tom Allen said that he had put up his own stake money for the Goss fight and now believed Eph Holland had used it against him.
Tom Allen claimed that in a fair fight he could have beaten Joe Goss in half an hour.
Eph Holland, a Cincinnati sporting man, was in charge of the affair for the fight between Tom Allen and Joe Goss.
Dad Ryan acted as Tom Allen's umpire in the fight, and Jack Brown acted as Joe Goss's umpire.
Joe Goss offered $1,000 on the result of the fight.
Tom Allen weighed 174 pounds for his fight with Joe Goss, who weighed 165 pounds.
Tom Allen covered a $1,000 wager from Joe Goss on the result of their fight.
Jack Looney of St. Louis arrived with a party of 25 men, saying Allen must be whipped.
Tom Kelly and Arthur Chambers were Tom Allen's seconds for the Goss fight.
Fred Watkins, backing Tom Allen at the Goss fight, handed a $1,000 bill to referee Eph Holland, who had made himself stakeholder.
A card by Tom Allen claimed it was impossible to obtain fair play in this country.
Tom Allen made the rounds of the Cincinnati hotels and then went into a saloon on Vine Street near Fourth Street while crowds waited outside.
Tom Allen weighed about 180 pounds after the Goss fight.
Tom Allen claimed he could beat Joe Goss.
Pat Mullins and J. Driscoll were Tom Allen's seconds in his glove fight with Tompkins Gilbert.
Tom Allen was in training at Barnet, on the Thames near London, in March 1878 under his trainer Jack Hopkins.
Tom Allen weighed fourteen stone, or 196 pounds, in training.
